Definition: from a compound of G4862 and κυρέω (to light or happen; from the base of G2962); concurrence, i.e. accident:--chance.
BiblicalUsage: By chance there comes down a certain priest that way, and when he sees the wounded man he passes by on the other side. The chance is the priest's excuse and the wounded man's tragedy: the very man who should have stopped is the one who happens by and keeps walking.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that there is no such thing as chance when a wounded man lies in the road, and I hold that passing by on the other side is a choice, not an accident.
